summary: Phase 149O.20J -- Class-B Deployment Verifier / Model-A Environment-Lock Independent Implementation Verification: INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION ONLY, no repair performed. Initial inspection confirmed repo clean, origin/main..HEAD=0, pcae health/check/status-coherence/push-check/runtime-inspect/notify-status all as expected, 149O.20I confirmed completed/reconciled via pcae phase-report reconcile --phase-id 149O.20I. Read docs/contracts/HATP_CLASS_B_DEPLOYMENT_CONTRACT.md and docs/contracts/HATP_MANDATORY_INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION_CERTIFICATION_CONTRACT.md directly, plus all three 149O.20I production modules (hatp_class_b_topology_verifier.py 707 lines, hatp_environment_lock_verifier.py 429 lines, hatp_class_b_conformance.py 163 lines) line-by-line from primary source -- never accepting 149O.20I's own report claims as the oracle. Independently reconstructed the phase-entry diff: existing HMIC-bound production files (hatp_bootstrap.py, repository_identity.py, hatp_mandatory_certification.py, hatp_mandatory_cutover.py, scripts/hatp_certification_admin.py) confirmed byte-unchanged since commit d3be5440 (149O.20F), predating 20H/20I entirely. Independently traced all HBDC-REQ requirement ownership from the actual check_id strings in the code, and adjudicated all 8 CBD invariants individually (not a summary-level pass): 6/8 clean, 2/8 (CBD-3 effective-access, CBD-6 environment lock) each carrying one of the Blocking findings below. Built an independent 62-test adversarial suite (tests/test_phase_149o_20j_class_b_deployment_verifier_model_a_environment_lock_independent_implementation_verification.py) with its own fixtures and helpers, never importing 149O.20I's own test constants/fixture builders as oracle: effective-permission logic (owner/no-access/world-writable/supplementary-group-write-grant/group-bit-without-membership, using a deterministic minimal trusted PATH to avoid this dev host's own real PATH making ACL-tooling resolution indeterminate), a two-depth ancestor-chain attack plus an explicit stop-boundary proof, a real os.link hard-link fixture, symlinked-ancestor rejection, ACL platform-unsupported fail-closed confirmation, a subprocess-isolated sys.meta_path class-based and instance-based hostile-finder re-attack (isolated from pytest's own AssertionRewritingHook), .pth path-injection and space-delimited-import-line rejection, a fake-Git-via-hostile-PATH attack and an agent-writable-PATH-directory-precedes-real-git attack, a from-scratch aggregator positive-all-satisfied fixture plus a full one-failure-at-5-positions/empty-check-set/missing-evidence/7-category-exception-injection matrix, a status/reason-separation proof, a zero-caller-authority inspect.signature sweep across every function in all three modules, real-host non-mutation snapshot verification (.pcae/, .pcae/hatp-evidence/, .pcae/repository-identity.json, docs/contracts/, plus git status --porcelain, before/after all three public API calls -- byte-identical), and a repository-wide zero-authority-consumer text search. Found and independently confirmed 3 Blocking-for-HMIC-binding-progression defects, recorded not repaired: (1) hatp_environment_lock_verifier.py's _check_pth_files (HBDC-REQ-031) detection predicate line.strip().startswith('import ') misses the tab-delimited 'import\t' form that real CPython site.addpackage() (verified directly against the running interpreter's own site module source) still executes -- independently demonstrated the exact bypass; (2) hatp_class_b_topology_verifier.py's _current_agent_identity never independently folds in os.getegid(), relying solely on os.getgroups(), which POSIX does not guarantee includes the process's true effective gid in every process-identity configuration -- a narrow but real fail-open gap in every group-membership-based effective-access check; (3) _resolve_trusted_executable (backing HBDC-REQ-038's trusted-Git resolution) deliberately uses only mode+group-bit checking, never the ACL-including _effective_write_access, to avoid unbounded recursion into getfacl resolution -- an ACL-only write grant to a PATH-preceding directory or the git executable itself would not be detected, a materially narrower guarantee than the Protected Root checks. Also independently re-verified both of 149O.20I's own self-caught defect fixes (sys.meta_path class-vs-instance identity bug; HBDC-REQ-004 environ false-positive narrowing) as correct. Confirmed zero production authority consumers of the three verifier modules anywhere in src/pcae/** (repository-wide search), zero references in hatp_mandatory_cutover.py/hatp_mandatory_certification.py/scripts/hatp_certification_admin.py, and the three modules' continued absence from HMIC's live 19-entry _FROZEN_SRC_PCAE_RELATIVE_FILES set (byte-for-byte cross-checked against hatp_environment_lock_verifier.py's own literal reproduction -- identical). Ran the repository-standard Fast Green suite raw (69 failed, 6720 passed, 5 skipped, 1 pre-existing fido2 collection error) and, to isolate this phase's own contribution, a freshly-reproduced baseline with this phase's one new test file temporarily removed (70 failed, 6657 passed, 4 skipped, 1 error) -- proving zero net-new failures attributable to this phase; the 1-failure swing matches the already-disclosed test_backend_cli.py parallel-execution flakiness category. All 69-70 failures independently spot-checked by node-ID category as exclusively historical phases' own pinned-requirement-count/pinned-commit-range self-checks (149O.14/15/16/18c/18d/19.2/19.3/19.3R/19.3R.1/19.4/19.5e-series/19.5f/19.5g/20c/20f/20g), the same disclosed debt category 149O.20I's own report already cited a subset of -- none reference the three new modules or any 20J-authored test. Ran a broad pytest -k 'class_b or hbdc or hmic or 149o_20' sweep (44 failed, 1107 passed, 5 skipped, ignoring the same pre-existing fido2 collection-error module) -- same debt category, zero net-new. Ran governance close checks (pcae health/check/status coherence/doctor task-memory/push check/runtime inspect/notify status) -- all as expected. Created a governed validation-mode task with production/contract/script files explicitly forbidden, before making any change, per this repository's established convention. Updated PROJECT_STATUS.md (demoting 149O.20I to a new 'Previous Phase' stacked entry) and CHANGELOG.md. Wrote docs/PHASE_149O_20J_CLASS_B_DEPLOYMENT_VERIFIER_MODEL_A_ENVIRONMENT_LOCK_INDEPENDENT_IMPLEMENTATION_VERIFICATION.md documenting the full baseline, diff reconstruction, HBDC traceability, CBD adjudication, attack reattack, result-model/status-vocabulary/signature/authority-derivation analysis, read-only static+behavioral verification, subprocess inventory, principal-separation/effective-permission/group/ACL/ancestor/symlink/hard-link analysis, environment-lock re-derivation, trusted-Git analysis, aggregator re-derivation, zero-authority-consumer proof, HMIC non-binding proof, CBV-S1/CBV-S10 status, self-caught-defect re-verification, real-host result/non-mutation, all findings, and the verification verdict. Verdict: CLASS-B DEPLOYMENT VERIFIER / MODEL-A ENVIRONMENT-LOCK -- NOT VERIFIED FOR HMIC-BINDING PROGRESSION (3 Blocking findings), but CURRENT NON-AUTHORITATIVE POSTURE INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED SAFE (read-only, fail-closed, zero production authority consumers, source not yet HMIC-bound). CBV-S1: current-state safety independently verified, binding requires the 3 findings repaired first, NOT CLOSED. CBV-S10: readiness integration contract gap remains, NOT CLOSED. Class-B remains CONTRACT VERIFIED -- VERIFIER IMPLEMENTATION INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED WITH 3 BLOCKING GAPS -- NOT PROVISIONED. HATP production remains NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable. This phase does not authorize real provisioning, certification, activation, HMIC scope evolution, or readiness integration, and did not repair any of the 3 findings it recorded. Recommended next phase: Phase 149O.20J.1 -- Class-B Deployment Verifier / Model-A Environment-Lock Narrow Defect Repair -- not authorized by this phase.
